description: We are Team Ninja Coder, a group of passionate tech enthusiasts ready to solve real-world challenges through innovation. For NASA Space Apps Challenge, we're building a health app to support astronauts' physical and mental well-being in space. We welcome creative problem-solvers with skills in app development, AI/ML, UI/UX design, healthcare research, and data analysis. If you love technology, teamwork, and space exploration, join us!
summary:
AstroGuard AI is an innovative astronaut health monitoring prototype designed to improve health awareness and preparedness during space missions.

Astronauts face unique challenges, including radiation exposure, isolation, altered gravity, and limited access to immediate medical assistance. Our solution addresses these challenges by combining health observations, simulated real-time vital signs, environmental monitoring, and explainable alerts within one interactive platform.

AstroGuard AI features a live dashboard, mission simulator, daily health check-ins, historical health records, and educational guidance informed by NASA's Human Research Program resources. Unlike basic monitoring dashboards, our system explains why certain readings may require attention through transparent, rule-based assessments.

The prototype uses fictional simulated data and is intended for educational demonstration, not medical diagnosis.

By making complex health information easier to understand, AstroGuard AI demonstrates how integrated monitoring could support astronaut wellbeing, improve mission preparedness, and inspire future space-health research and remote healthcare applications on Earth.
details:
What Does Our Project Do?

AstroGuard AI is a functional astronaut health monitoring software prototype developed to improve health awareness during space missions. It brings health observations, simulated real-time vital signs, environmental conditions, and explainable alerts together in one interactive platform.

Astronauts face unique challenges, including radiation exposure, isolation, altered gravity, and limited access to immediate medical assistance. Our project explores how technology can make health information easier to monitor, interpret, and understand in these challenging environments.

How Does It Work?

AstroGuard AI follows three main steps: Monitor → Assess → Explain.

  1. Monitor: An interactive dashboard displays simulated heart rate, oxygen saturation, body temperature, cabin carbon dioxide levels, and radiation readings. Astronaut profiles and daily health check-ins allow users to record additional observations, including sleep and stress.
  2. Assess: The system evaluates observations using predefined, rule-based assessments to identify readings that may require attention.
  3. Explain: Instead of displaying unexplained warnings, AstroGuard AI provides understandable alerts that explain why a particular observation was flagged.

The platform also stores health records in a SQLite database, allowing users to review previous observations and track changes over time.

Additionally, it includes educational information about NASA's five hazards of human spaceflight.

Benefits and Intended Impact

Our goal is to demonstrate how integrated and understandable health information could support astronaut health awareness and mission preparedness.

AstroGuard AI could inspire future research into monitoring tools that help astronauts and mission teams recognize changes, review health trends, and understand potential concerns more efficiently.

Beyond space exploration, similar concepts could have educational and research applications in remote healthcare, including underserved regions where access to specialist medical support is limited.

Technologies Used

We developed AstroGuard AI using:

  • React, Vite, and Tailwind CSS for the interactive frontend and responsive dashboard.
  • Python and FastAPI for backend services, health assessments, and API communication.
  • SQLite for persistent storage of astronaut profiles, health check-ins, and monitoring history.
  • JavaScript for frontend functionality and interactive visualizations.
  • Git and GitHub for version control and team collaboration.

Our current prototype uses simulated sensor readings rather than physical monitoring hardware or real astronaut medical data.

What Makes Our Project Creative?

AstroGuard AI combines health monitoring, environmental awareness, explainable assessments, historical records, and spaceflight education in one accessible platform.

Its key feature is explainability. Instead of simply showing measurements or generating warnings, the system communicates why an observation may need attention.

The interactive mission simulator also allows users to explore changing conditions without requiring expensive hardware or access to sensitive astronaut health information.

Factors We Considered

During development, our team focused on usability, transparency, data persistence, scientific relevance, and responsible communication of health information.

We used NASA Human Research Program resources to understand the challenges astronauts face. We also designed our prototype around fictional simulated data to avoid presenting unverified measurements as real medical evidence.

Although our project is named AstroGuard AI, its current assessments use transparent, rule-based logic rather than a trained machine-learning model. It is an educational and research-oriented prototype, not a clinically validated medical device.

Our Future Vision

We hope to expand AstroGuard AI by integrating real sensor hardware, exploring validated health datasets, and researching more advanced predictive models.

Our vision is to make astronaut health information more connected, understandable, and accessible, contributing to safer and better-prepared future space exploration.
